# EventCatalog

> EventCatalog is an Open Source project that helps you document your messages, services and domains.

- [EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/index.md)

## about-us

The story behind EventCatalog - an open source project built to bring discoverability to your architecture.

- [The Story Behind EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/about-us.md): The story behind EventCatalog - an open source project built to bring discoverability to your architecture.

## blog

Blog

- [Blog  -  EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog.md): Blog

### 2026

- [Introducing diagrams as first-class resources](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/2026/01/09/diagrams-as-first-class-resources.md): EventCatalog already gives you auto-generated visualizations: Entity Maps, Interaction Maps, and domain views that update as your catalog changes. These are great for understanding relationships between your resources.

### api-catalog

EventCatalog can now publish an API catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog, giving agents and developer tools one machine-readable place to discover your service, domain, and MCP API surfaces.

- [Let tools find your APIs from one URL](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/api-catalog.md): EventCatalog can now publish an API catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog, giving agents and developer tools one machine-readable place to discover your service, domain, and MCP API surfaces.

### apicurio-registry-eventcatalog

Connect Apicurio Registry to EventCatalog for better schema governance and documentation

- [Integrate Apicurio Registry with EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/apicurio-registry-eventcatalog.md): Connect Apicurio Registry to EventCatalog for better schema governance and documentation

### architecture-change-detection

Architecture Change Detection in EventCatalog monitors your event-driven architecture across git branches and notifies your teams the moment a service starts or stops producing or consuming messages.

- [Your architecture is changing. Do you know about it?](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/architecture-change-detection.md): Architecture Change Detection in EventCatalog monitors your event-driven architecture across git branches and notifies your teams the moment a service starts or stops producing or consuming messages.

Connect AI tools to your architecture with 15 tools and 9 resources

### bundled-docs-for-coding-agents

EventCatalog 3.35.1 bundles the full documentation inside the npm package itself, giving AI coding agents a version-matched source of truth they can read before touching your catalog.

- [Giving your AI agents docs they can actually trust](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/bundled-docs-for-coding-agents.md): EventCatalog 3.35.1 bundles the full documentation inside the npm package itself, giving AI coding agents a version-matched source of truth they can read before touching your catalog.

### c4-and-eventcatalog

Two ways to bring C4 architecture modeling into EventCatalog: a Claude skill that converts C4 diagrams (Structurizr, C4-PlantUML, Mermaid C4) into a full event-driven catalog, and the LikeC4 component that renders interactive C4 diagrams directly inside EventCatalog pages.

- [How to turn C4 diagrams into EventCatalog documentation](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/c4-and-eventcatalog.md): Two ways to bring C4 architecture modeling into EventCatalog: a Claude skill that converts C4 diagrams (Structurizr, C4-PlantUML, Mermaid C4) into a full event-driven catalog, and the LikeC4 component that renders interactive C4 diagrams directly inside EventCatalog pages.

### channels-20

Introducing EventCatalog 2.65.0 with support for channels 2.0

- [Modelling more message patterns in EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/channels-20.md): Introducing EventCatalog 2.65.0 with support for channels 2.0

### custom-icons

EventCatalog 3.28.1 lets you set a custom icon on any resource. One field in frontmatter and your visualiser goes from generic coloured boxes to a diagram that tells the real story of your stack.

- [Your catalog nodes now show what they actually are](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/custom-icons.md): EventCatalog 3.28.1 lets you set a custom icon on any resource. One field in frontmatter and your visualiser goes from generic coloured boxes to a diagram that tells the real story of your stack.

### custom-search-experience

EventCatalog introduces a completely redesigned search experience with advanced filtering, categorized results, and instant discovery for static builds. Find domains, services, events, and documentation faster than ever.

- [Introducing Search v2](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/custom-search-experience.md): EventCatalog introduces a completely redesigned search experience with advanced filtering, categorized results, and instant discovery for static builds. Find domains, services, events, and documentation faster than ever.

### data-products

Data products join EventCatalog as a first-class resource type with inputs, outputs, contracts, and full integration with your existing architecture.

- [Document, visualize and discover your data products](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/data-products.md): Data products join EventCatalog as a first-class resource type with inputs, outputs, contracts, and full integration with your existing architecture.

### document-ai-agents

EventCatalog 3.41.0 adds first-class agent documentation so teams can reduce agent sprawl, track ownership, see model and tool usage, and understand how agents consume and produce information across their architecture.

- [Document and Govern AI Agents in EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/document-ai-agents.md): EventCatalog 3.41.0 adds first-class agent documentation so teams can reduce agent sprawl, track ownership, see model and tool usage, and understand how agents consume and produce information across their architecture.

### documenting-sync-and-async-apis-with-eventcatalog

Learn how EventCatalog's OpenAPI and AsyncAPI generators help companies bridge the gap between synchronous REST APIs and asynchronous event-driven architectures

- [Documenting sync and async APIs with EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/documenting-sync-and-async-apis-with-eventcatalog.md): Learn how EventCatalog's OpenAPI and AsyncAPI generators help companies bridge the gap between synchronous REST APIs and asynchronous event-driven architectures

### external-systems

A new externalSystem flag lets you mark services like Stripe, Twilio, or Snowflake as third-party dependencies. They get their own colour, their own sidebar section, and their own tab in discover.

- [Model external systems in EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/external-systems.md): A new externalSystem flag lets you mark services like Stripe, Twilio, or Snowflake as third-party dependencies. They get their own colour, their own sidebar section, and their own tab in discover.

### field-usage

EventCatalog already shows you which services consume a message. Now it can also show you which specific fields they use.

- [Which fields are your consumers actually using?](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/field-usage.md): EventCatalog already shows you which services consume a message. Now it can also show you which specific fields they use.

### flow-containers-and-data-products

EventCatalog v3.36.3 adds two new flow node types, containers and data products, so you can model the full journey from services and events through to data stores and analytical products in a single diagram.

- [Flows now support containers and data products](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/flow-containers-and-data-products.md): EventCatalog v3.36.3 adds two new flow node types, containers and data products, so you can model the full journey from services and events through to data stores and analytical products in a single diagram.

### flow-wizard

The new flow-wizard skill lets you describe a business workflow in plain language while your AI agent builds the flow and wires it to your existing catalog resources.

- [Describe the workflow, let the agent build the flow](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/flow-wizard.md): The new flow-wizard skill lets you describe a business workflow in plain language while your AI agent builds the flow and wires it to your existing catalog resources.

### github-as-a-schema-registry

EventCatalog now supports GitHub as a schema registry, allowing you to document your schemas in GitHub and keep them in sync with your documentation.

- [Using GitHub as a schema registry with EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/github-as-a-schema-registry.md): EventCatalog now supports GitHub as a schema registry, allowing you to document your schemas in GitHub and keep them in sync with your documentation.

### indexed-search

EventCatalog v3.36.0 adds indexed full-content search powered by Pagefind. One config line is all you need to search message bodies, changelogs, and custom docs alongside every resource in your catalog.

- [Full-content search comes to EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/indexed-search.md): EventCatalog v3.36.0 adds indexed full-content search powered by Pagefind. One config line is all you need to search message bodies, changelogs, and custom docs alongside every resource in your catalog.

### introducing-adrs

Architecture Decision Records are now a first-class resource in EventCatalog. Document the why behind your design choices and link them directly to the services, events, and domains they affect.

- [Your architecture decisions belong next to your architecture](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/introducing-adrs.md): Architecture Decision Records are now a first-class resource in EventCatalog. Document the why behind your design choices and link them directly to the services, events, and domains they affect.

### message-usage-examples

Message Usage Examples lets you ship real payload samples alongside your events, commands, and queries so your team never has to guess what an OrderCreated event actually looks like in production.

- [Document examples with your schemas](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/message-usage-examples.md): Message Usage Examples lets you ship real payload samples alongside your events, commands, and queries so your team never has to guess what an OrderCreated event actually looks like in production.

### openapi-consumer-services

The EventCatalog OpenAPI generator now lets you define consumer services with optional route-based filtering, so you can document the full producer-consumer picture directly from your OpenAPI specs.

- [Document who consumes your APIs, not just who owns them](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/openapi-consumer-services.md): The EventCatalog OpenAPI generator now lets you define consumer services with optional route-based filtering, so you can document the full producer-consumer picture directly from your OpenAPI specs.

### prompt-and-visibility-components

EventCatalog 3.33.0 ships two new MDX components, Prompt and Visibility, that turn your catalog into a dual-audience documentation layer without forking content.

- [Write docs once, serve both humans and AI agents](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/prompt-and-visibility-components.md): EventCatalog 3.33.0 ships two new MDX components, Prompt and Visibility, that turn your catalog into a dual-audience documentation layer without forking content.

### remote-schema-component

EventCatalog 2.52.0 introduces the RemoteSchema component, enabling real-time schema synchronization from external APIs and keeping your documentation always up-to-date.

- [Introducing Remote Schemas - Fetch and Sync Schemas at Runtime](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/remote-schema-component.md): EventCatalog 2.52.0 introduces the RemoteSchema component, enabling real-time schema synchronization from external APIs and keeping your documentation always up-to-date.

### resource-docs

Stop losing documentation in wikis and Confluence pages. Resource-level documentation lets you attach runbooks, ADRs, guides, and more directly to the services, events, and domains they describe.

- [The right documentation, in the right place](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/resource-docs.md): Stop losing documentation in wikis and Confluence pages. Resource-level documentation lets you attach runbooks, ADRs, guides, and more directly to the services, events, and domains they describe.

### schema-features

- [EventCatalog 2.64.0 - Schemas!](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/schema-features.md): EventCatalog Schema updates

### schema-fields-explorer

EventCatalog now indexes every field from every message schema and lets you search, filter, and trace fields across your entire architecture. Scale plan users get Field Intelligence with type conflict detection and interactive traceability graphs.

- [Trace every field across your schemas and architecture](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog/schema-fields-explorer.md): EventCatalog now indexes every field from every message schema and lets you search, filter, and trace fields across your entire architecture. Scale plan users get Field Intelligence with type conflict detection and interactive traceability graphs.

### slack-integration

### sync-users-from-github

### live-data-meets-architecture-documentation

Extend EventCatalog Assistant with custom tools to bring real-time metrics, service health, on-call information, and more into your architecture conversations

- [Live data meets architecture documentation](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/live-data-meets-architecture-documentation.md): Extend EventCatalog Assistant with custom tools to bring real-time metrics, service health, on-call information, and more into your architecture conversations

### message-usage-examples

Message Usage Examples lets you ship real payload samples alongside your events, commands, and queries so your team never has to guess what an OrderCreated event actually looks like in production.

- [Document examples with your schemas](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/message-usage-examples.md): Message Usage Examples lets you ship real payload samples alongside your events, commands, and queries so your team never has to guess what an OrderCreated event actually looks like in production.

### openapi-consumer-services

The EventCatalog OpenAPI generator now lets you define consumer services with optional route-based filtering, so you can document the full producer-consumer picture directly from your OpenAPI specs.

- [Document who consumes your APIs, not just who owns them](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/openapi-consumer-services.md): The EventCatalog OpenAPI generator now lets you define consumer services with optional route-based filtering, so you can document the full producer-consumer picture directly from your OpenAPI specs.

### prompt-and-visibility-components

EventCatalog 3.33.0 ships two new MDX components, Prompt and Visibility, that turn your catalog into a dual-audience documentation layer without forking content.

- [Write docs once, serve both humans and AI agents](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/prompt-and-visibility-components.md): EventCatalog 3.33.0 ships two new MDX components, Prompt and Visibility, that turn your catalog into a dual-audience documentation layer without forking content.

### remote-schema-component

EventCatalog 2.52.0 introduces the RemoteSchema component, enabling real-time schema synchronization from external APIs and keeping your documentation always up-to-date.

- [Introducing Remote Schemas - Fetch and Sync Schemas at Runtime](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/remote-schema-component.md): EventCatalog 2.52.0 introduces the RemoteSchema component, enabling real-time schema synchronization from external APIs and keeping your documentation always up-to-date.

### resource-docs

Stop losing documentation in wikis and Confluence pages. Resource-level documentation lets you attach runbooks, ADRs, guides, and more directly to the services, events, and domains they describe.

- [The right documentation, in the right place](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/resource-docs.md): Stop losing documentation in wikis and Confluence pages. Resource-level documentation lets you attach runbooks, ADRs, guides, and more directly to the services, events, and domains they describe.

### schema-features

EventCatalog Schema updates

- [EventCatalog 2.64.0 - Schemas!](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/schema-features.md): EventCatalog Schema updates

### schema-fields-explorer

EventCatalog now indexes every field from every message schema and lets you search, filter, and trace fields across your entire architecture. Scale plan users get Field Intelligence with type conflict detection and interactive traceability graphs.

- [Trace every field across your schemas and architecture](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/schema-fields-explorer.md): EventCatalog now indexes every field from every message schema and lets you search, filter, and trace fields across your entire architecture. Scale plan users get Field Intelligence with type conflict detection and interactive traceability graphs.

### slack-integration

Stop searching through wikis and Confluence pages. Get architecture answers where your team already works.

- [EventCatalog Slack integration](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/slack-integration.md): Stop searching through wikis and Confluence pages. Get architecture answers where your team already works.

### sync-users-from-github

EventCatalog can now sync users and teams directly from GitHub. Point it at your org, and ownership data stays accurate without manual upkeep.

- [Sync users and teams from GitHub into EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/sync-users-from-github.md): EventCatalog can now sync users and teams directly from GitHub. Point it at your org, and ownership data stays accurate without manual upkeep.

### visualizer-improvements

The EventCatalog visualizer just got a complete overhaul. Cleaner nodes, smarter layouts, dark mode support, hover highlighting and more.

- [See your architecture clearly: Major visualizer improvements](https://eventcatalog.dev/blog-2/visualizer-improvements.md): The EventCatalog visualizer just got a complete overhaul. Cleaner nodes, smarter layouts, dark mode support, hover highlighting and more.

## use-cases

Different ways teams use EventCatalog to document, govern, and evolve their architecture.

- [Common patterns with EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases.md): Different ways teams use EventCatalog to document, govern, and evolve their architecture.

### ai-engineering-context

Give your AI assistants and agents the architectural context they need to reason about your domains, services, events, and schemas.

- [Context for AI engineering](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/ai-engineering-context.md): Give your AI assistants and agents the architectural context they need to reason about your domains, services, events, and schemas.

### ai-llm-context-foundation

Give your AI assistants the architectural context they need. EventCatalog becomes the source of truth that LLMs can query to understand your domains, services, events, and organizational boundaries.

- [AI/LLM Context Foundation](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/ai-llm-context-foundation.md): Give your AI assistants the architectural context they need. EventCatalog becomes the source of truth that LLMs can query to understand your domains, services, events, and organizational boundaries.

### architecture-documentation

Document your software architecture with a tool designed specifically for software primitives. Bring all your architecture artifacts into one place, version them with Git, and make them discoverable for humans and AI.

- [Architecture Documentation](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/architecture-documentation.md): Document your software architecture with a tool designed specifically for software primitives. Bring all your architecture artifacts into one place, version them with Git, and make them discoverable for humans and AI.

### architecture-planning

Plan your future architecture alongside your current state. Use drafts, versioning, and visual comparison to design changes before writing code.

- [Architecture Planning](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/architecture-planning.md): Plan your future architecture alongside your current state. Use drafts, versioning, and visual comparison to design changes before writing code.

### automated-catalog

Automate your architecture documentation from schema registries, OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, custom tooling, and AI.

- [Automated catalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/automated-catalog.md): Automate your architecture documentation from schema registries, OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, custom tooling, and AI.

### automated-documentation

Sync documentation from your OpenAPI and AsyncAPI specs. Automate what changes, keep manual control over business context.

- [Automated Documentation](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/automated-documentation.md): Sync documentation from your OpenAPI and AsyncAPI specs. Automate what changes, keep manual control over business context.

### beyond-api-documentation

EventCatalog is more than an API documentation tool. Capture business context, flows, domains, team ownership, and ubiquitous language alongside your technical specifications.

- [Not Just an API Documentation Tool](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/beyond-api-documentation.md): EventCatalog is more than an API documentation tool. Capture business context, flows, domains, team ownership, and ubiquitous language alongside your technical specifications.

### breaking-change-detection

Understand the downstream impact of schema changes before they reach production. Visualize consumers, detect breaking changes with AI, and coordinate changes across distributed teams.

- [Breaking Change Detection](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/breaking-change-detection.md): Understand the downstream impact of schema changes before they reach production. Visualize consumers, detect breaking changes with AI, and coordinate changes across distributed teams.

### ci-cd-integration

Integrate EventCatalog into your CI/CD pipelines. Rebuild your catalog automatically when schemas change, on a schedule, or on demand.

- [CI/CD Integration](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/ci-cd-integration.md): Integrate EventCatalog into your CI/CD pipelines. Rebuild your catalog automatically when schemas change, on a schedule, or on demand.

### custom-governance

EventCatalog is technology-agnostic and lives as docs as code—so you can shape governance workflows to fit your architecture, not the other way around.

- [Custom governance workflows](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/custom-governance.md): EventCatalog is technology-agnostic and lives as docs as code—so you can shape governance workflows to fit your architecture, not the other way around.

### domain-driven-design

Document your domain model with first-class support for domains, bounded contexts, ubiquitous language, and team ownership. Map business context to technical implementation.

- [Domain-Driven Design Documentation](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/domain-driven-design.md): Document your domain model with first-class support for domains, bounded contexts, ubiquitous language, and team ownership. Map business context to technical implementation.

### federated-catalog

- [Federated catalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/federated-catalog.md): Teams own their own catalogs and federate them into one central catalog for organization-wide visibility.

### schema-documentation

Transform technical schemas into business-contextualized documentation. Sync from any source, enrich with ownership and purpose, track changes over time.

- [Enrich Schemas with Documentation](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/schema-documentation.md): Transform technical schemas into business-contextualized documentation. Sync from any source, enrich with ownership and purpose, track changes over time.

### shared-understanding

Build a shared understanding of your architecture across engineering, product, and business teams—domains, ubiquitous language, services, diagrams, and business workflows in one tool.

- [A shared understanding across the organization](https://eventcatalog.dev/use-cases/shared-understanding.md): Build a shared understanding of your architecture across engineering, product, and business teams—domains, ubiquitous language, services, diagrams, and business workflows in one tool.

### tutorial

Learn what you will build in the EventCatalog tutorial.

- [Introduction](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial.md): Learn what you will build in the EventCatalog tutorial.
- [Add ownership](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/add-ownership.md): Create a team and assign it to your services and event.
- [Build and deploy your catalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/build-your-catalog.md): Build your EventCatalog site and choose a deployment path.
- [Consume the event from a service](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/consume-event.md): Create InventoryService and mark it as a consumer of OrderPlaced.
- [Create a domain](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/create-a-domain.md): Group the tutorial services into a domain.
- [Create a service](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/create-a-service.md): Add the first service to your tutorial catalog.
- [Create an event](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/create-event.md): Add the first event and schema to your tutorial catalog.
- [Install EventCatalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/install-eventcatalog.md): Create a new EventCatalog project from the command line.
- [Next steps](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/next-steps.md): Grow your catalog beyond the tutorial.
- [Publish the event from a service](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/publish-event.md): Update OrderService so EventCatalog knows it publishes OrderPlaced.
- [Visualize your catalog](https://eventcatalog.dev/docs/tutorial/visualize-your-catalog.md): Use EventCatalog visualizations to inspect the tutorial architecture.
